Sam: Heads-up — after the kernel selector rollout to canary, host ingress p99 jumped ~10% for small requests. Traced one host over 3m. Link: https://go/redwood/issue/1234
Angela: Which exact path? pre-tokenizer or stream coalescer? :eyes:
Sam: Pre-token stream path — the code that does micro-parse + coalesce on readv. Repro: run a ~1k qps small-payload canary and look at host decode tail.
Devon: Pulled trace 3055... seeing a burst of context switches in pretoken worker and lots of `kv_cache.lookup` stalls. Quick excerpt from host logs:
Devon: ```
[host] pretoken: readv 0.9ms -> parse 1.8ms -> kvcache.lookup 4.2ms (hot)
[host] handler: dispatch 0.6ms -> grpc_writev 0.5ms
```
Mira: Hmm. The kernel selector change bumped batch hints; could be extra kernel init on tiny batches + kvcache churn. Also noticing more small syscalls on the gRPC path.
Sam: Right — p99 increase correlates with writev count rising. Suspect fragmentation + extra allocations in pretoken stage.
Angela: Can someone run the lightweight sampler with `--pretoken-skip` to isolate tokenization overhead? Also set `KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1` on the node.
Devon: I ran a short AB with those flags: skipping pretoken reduced p99 by ~6%, but kvcache miss rate stayed roughly the same (so separate issue).
ci-bot: perf-ci: nightly-run/3055 finished — unit tests ok; perf report shows host_ingress_p99 +9.7% for canary cohort. Dashboard: https://go/redwood/perf/3055 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Mira: Proposed next steps: 1) revert batch-hint tweak in kernel selector for canary, 2) instrument readv/writev counts and small-allocation churn, 3) collect top-5 kvcache callers heatmap. I'll take (3) and add more granular traces.
Sam: Assigning @Mira and @Devon for triage. I'll draft a quick PR to gate the selector change if we see >5% p99 regression across more hosts.
Devon: Repro script (local): `scripts/repro/host-smallreq-canary --qps=1000 --payload=64 --duration=120`
Angela: +1. If revert is needed, re-enable previous selector binary for canary tier and monitor for tail recovery.
Sam: Thanks — please post any new traces here. I'll update the incident board after the first mitigation step. :thumbsup:
